newsitem.title: USA: U.S. BULK MILLFEEDS - DEALERS EYE CBOT CORN RUNUP.
newsitem.headline: U.S. BULK MILLFEEDS - DEALERS EYE CBOT CORN RUNUP.

text.p: U.S. millfeed prices were mixed on Tuesday as dealers across the United States watched the sharp runup in Chicago Board of Trade corn futures.
The strength in CBOT corn has contributed to the increase in spot midd prices, a Buffalo dealer said.
CBOT corn futures were locked up their 12-cent trading limit at midsession on a bullish U.S. Department of Agriculture August crop production report, traders said.
Buffalo spot prices were bid at $70 a ton and offered at $75 a ton, up $3 and $5 respectively.
"But I don't think the feedmixers have quite caught up with that yet," the Buffalo dealer said.

A North Carolina dealer said the corn rally has pushed midd offerings higher but bids have not gone up. He viewed this as a negative for the market because buyers would turn to cheaper substitutes for their ingredients like soyhull.

On the other hand, a Kansas dealer said the corn rally would probably help the midds market. "If corn is 20 cents higher when the smoke clears, theoretically midds would be worth a couple dollars more," he said.
